claim: For all proteins tested, the streptavidin signal was significantly stronger than an antibody signal.
source: For all proteins tested, the streptavidin signal was significantly stronger than an antibody signal, markedly improving the sensitivity of expansion microscopy and correlative light and electron microscopy.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a general finding across all tested proteins, supported by experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Streptavidin imaging markedly improves the sensitivity of expansion microscopy.
source: For all proteins tested, the streptavidin signal was significantly stronger than an antibody signal, markedly improving the sensitivity of expansion microscopy and correlative light and electron microscopy.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing streptavidin detection in expansion microscopy experiments.

claim: Streptavidin imaging markedly improves the sensitivity of correlative light and electron microscopy.
source: For all proteins tested, the streptavidin signal was significantly stronger than an antibody signal, markedly improving the sensitivity of expansion microscopy and correlative light and electron microscopy.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing streptavidin detection in CLEM experiments.

claim: Proteins within phase-separated regions such as the central channel of the nuclear pores were readily detected with streptavidin.
source: Importantly, proteins within phase-separated regions, such as the central channel of the nuclear pores, the nucleolus, or RNA granules, were readily detected with streptavidin, while most antibodies failed.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing streptavidin detection of proteins in nuclear pores.

claim: Proteins within the nucleolus were readily detected with streptavidin.
source: Importantly, proteins within phase-separated regions, such as the central channel of the nuclear pores, the nucleolus, or RNA granules, were readily detected with streptavidin, while most antibodies failed.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing streptavidin detection of nucleolar proteins.

claim: Proteins within RNA granules were readily detected with streptavidin.
source: Importantly, proteins within phase-separated regions, such as the central channel of the nuclear pores, the nucleolus, or RNA granules, were readily detected with streptavidin, while most antibodies failed.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing streptavidin detection of proteins in RNA granules.

claim: Most antibodies failed to detect proteins within phase-separated regions.
source: Importantly, proteins within phase-separated regions, such as the central channel of the nuclear pores, the nucleolus, or RNA granules, were readily detected with streptavidin, while most antibodies failed.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing absence of antibody signals in phase-separated regions.

claim: Co-probing with streptavidin and anti-HA can map antibody-accessibility when TurboID is used in tandem with an HA epitope tag.
source: When TurboID is used in tandem with an HA epitope tag, co-probing with streptavidin and anti-HA can map antibody-accessibility and we created such a map for the trypanosome nuclear pore.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing differential detection patterns between streptavidin and anti-HA.

claim: An antibody-accessibility map was created for the trypanosome nuclear pore.
source: When TurboID is used in tandem with an HA epitope tag, co-probing with streptavidin and anti-HA can map antibody-accessibility and we created such a map for the trypanosome nuclear pore.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing systematic mapping of all nuclear pore proteins.

claim: Streptavidin imaging resolves dynamic, temporally, and spatially distinct sub-complexes.
source: Lastly, we show that streptavidin imaging resolves dynamic, temporally, and spatially distinct sub-complexes and, in specific cases, reveals a history of dynamic protein interaction.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing streptavidin detection of proteins at different cellular locations over time.

claim: Streptavidin imaging reveals a history of dynamic protein interaction in specific cases.
source: Lastly, we show that streptavidin imaging resolves dynamic, temporally, and spatially distinct sub-complexes and, in specific cases, reveals a history of dynamic protein interaction.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing biotinylation patterns reflecting past protein interactions.

claim: Fluorescence is lost under fixation and permeabilisation conditions for fluorescent proteins.
source: Fluorescent proteins are not suitable for all imaging applications, because fluorescence is lost under fixation and permeabilisation conditions.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the limitations of fluorescent proteins.

claim: Correlative electron and light microscopy is fully dependent on antibodies.
source: Applications that are fully dependent on antibodies include correlative electron and light microscopy (CLEM) applications, expansion microscopy, or protein detection in combination with in situ hybridisation for nucleic acid detection.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about CLEM methodology.

claim: Expansion microscopy is fully dependent on antibodies.
source: Applications that are fully dependent on antibodies include correlative electron and light microscopy (CLEM) applications, expansion microscopy, or protein detection in combination with in situ hybridisation for nucleic acid detection.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about expansion microscopy methodology.

claim: Anti-HA antibody signal for endogenously expressed trypanosome MEX67 fused to HA was entirely restricted to the nucleoplasm.
source: We recently observed the absence of an anti-HA antibody signal at the nuclear pores for endogenously expressed trypanosome mRNA export factor MEX67 fused to the small peptide hemagglutinin (HA) epitope tag: the anti-HA signal was entirely restricted to the nucleoplasm (Moreira do et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by previously published data and cited.

claim: A polyclonal antibody raised against T. brucei MEX67 did not stain the nuclear pores.
source: Likewise, a polyclonal antibody raised against T. brucei MEX67 did not stain the nuclear pores (Pozzi et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by cited published data.

claim: Fusions of T. brucei MEX67 to fluorescent proteins are primarily detected at the nuclear pores with some signal extending to the nucleoplasm.
source: In contrast, fusions of T. brucei MEX67 to fluorescent proteins (either N- or C-terminally) are primarily detected at the nuclear pores with some signal extending to the nucleoplasm (Billington et al., 2023; Kramer et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by cited published data.

claim: T. brucei MEX67 functions in mRNA export.
source: This is in agreement with the reported function of T. brucei MEX67 in mRNA export (Dostalova et al., 2013; Schwede et al., 2009)
evidence: This is supported by cited published data.

claim: MEX67 orthologues localize to nuclear pores in other eukaryotes.
source: and with nuclear pore localisation of MEX67 orthologues in other eukaryotes (Katahira et al., 1999; Köhler and Hurt, 2007; Mangus et al., 2003; Rodriguez et al., 2004; Stewart, 2019; Strässer et al., 2000; Terry and Wente, 2007)
evidence: This is supported by multiple cited published studies.

claim: Mex67 was termed a mobile nucleoporin.
source: where Mex67 was even termed a mobile nucleoporin (Derrer et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by cited published data.

claim: TurboID is a biotin ligase widely employed for proximity labelling techniques facilitating analysis of protein interactions in vivo.
source: TurboID is a biotin ligase, widely employed for proximity labelling techniques facilitating analysis of protein interactions in vivo (Branon et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge about TurboID, supported by citation.

claim: Fluorophore labelled streptavidin delivered a signal localizing MEX67 primarily to the nuclear pores and partially to the nucleoplasm.
source: To our surprise, fluorophore labelled streptavidin readily delivered a signal localizing primarily to the nuclear pores and partially to the nucleoplasm, consistent with the localisation of MEX67 fused to fluorescent proteins (Moreira do et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and cited publication.

claim: The streptavidin signal shows the correct localisation of MEX67, while antibodies fail to bind MEX67 at the nuclear pore.
source: We, therefore, concluded that the streptavidin signal shows the correct localisation of MEX67, while antibodies fail to bind MEX67 at the nuclear pore and selectively stain the nucleoplasmic fraction of MEX67.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental observations and comparison with fluorescent protein data.

claim: MEX67 localizes to the central channel of the nuclear pore that is lined by phenylalanine-glycine nucleoporins (FG NUPs).
source: One possible reason for the absence of antibody stain could be the localisation of MEX67 to the central channel of the nuclear pore that is lined by phenylalanine-glycine nucleoporins (FG NUPs), intrinsically disordered proteins dominated by FG-repeats, that assemble to a dense meshwork and create a phase-separated environment, physically distinct from the rest of the cell (Davis et al., 2022; Nag et al., 2022).
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on known properties of nuclear pores, supported by citations.

claim: FG NUPs are intrinsically disordered proteins dominated by FG-repeats that assemble to a dense meshwork and create a phase-separated environment.
source: One possible reason for the absence of antibody stain could be the localisation of MEX67 to the central channel of the nuclear pore that is lined by phenylalanine-glycine nucleoporins (FG NUPs), intrinsically disordered proteins dominated by FG-repeats, that assemble to a dense meshwork and create a phase-separated environment, physically distinct from the rest of the cell (Davis et al., 2022; Nag et al., 2022).
evidence: This is established knowledge about FG NUPs, supported by citations.

claim: Tetrameric streptavidin is smaller and more compact than IgGs (60 kDa versus a tandem of two IgGs, each with 150 kDa).
source: It remains unclear, why streptavidin was able to stain biotinylated proteins within these antibody inaccessible regions, but possible reasons are: (i) tetrameric streptavidin is smaller and more compact than IgGs (60 kDa versus a tandem of two IgGs, each with 150 kDa)
evidence: This is established knowledge about the molecular weights of streptavidin and IgGs.

claim: The interaction between streptavidin and biotin is ~100 fold stronger than a typical interaction between antibody and antigen.
source: (ii) the interaction between streptavidin and biotin is ~100 fold stronger than a typical interaction between antibody and antigen
evidence: This is established knowledge about binding affinities.

claim: Streptavidin contains four fluorophores, in contrast to only one per secondary IgG.
source: and (iii) streptavidin contains four fluorophores, in contrast to only one per secondary IgG.
evidence: This is a property of the fluorophore-conjugated reagents used.

claim: 11 trypanosome proteins and one mammalian protein of different bona fide phase-separated regions were expressed fused to a TurboID-HA tandem tag.
source: We expressed 11 trypanosomes and one mammalian protein of different bona fide phase-separated regions (nucleolus, stress granules, central channel of the nuclear pores) fused to a TurboID-HA tandem tag.
evidence: This describes the experimental design.

claim: All tested proteins from phase-separated regions could be readily visualised with streptavidin.
source: All proteins could be readily visualised with streptavidin, while they could not be labelled with anti-HA.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data.

claim: Tested proteins from phase-separated regions could not be labelled with anti-HA.
source: All proteins could be readily visualised with streptavidin, while they could not be labelled with anti-HA.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data.

claim: The multiple biotinylation sites of the bait and adjacent proteins provide a massive boost in signal.
source: Importantly, we noticed that streptavidin imaging has further major advantages to antibody labeling, even for antibody-accessible proteins: (i) the multiple biotinylation sites of the bait and adjacent proteins provided a massive boost in signal, which is in particular useful in applications with diluted antigens, such as expansion microscopy or correlative light and electron microscopy (CLEM);
evidence: This is supported by experimental observations.

claim: Biotinylation extends to adjacent proteins and is stable over the lifetime of a protein.
source: (ii) since biotinylation extends to adjacent proteins and is stable over the lifetime of a protein, protein interactions are preserved in time, enabling to monitor dynamic processes in the cell.
evidence: This is based on known properties of biotinylation and experimental observations.

claim: T. brucei nuclear pore proteins NUP110, NUP76, and NUP96 were expressed fused to a TurboID-HA tandem tag in procyclic Trypanosoma brucei cells using both N and C-terminal fusion.
source: To establish a robust imaging system for TurboID fusion proteins by streptavidin, we expressed the T. brucei nuclear pore proteins NUP110, NUP76, and NUP96 fused to a TurboID-HA tandem tag in procyclic Trypanosoma brucei cells using both N and C-terminal fusion for each respective target protein.
evidence: This describes the experimental design.

claim: Expression of TurboID-HA fusion proteins was constitutive from the endogenous locus.
source: Expression was constitutive from the endogenous locus and labelling relied on the biotin substate present in the medium (0.8 µM in SDM79) (Moreira do et al., 2023).
evidence: This describes the experimental design.

claim: Labelling relied on the biotin substrate present in the medium (0.8 µM in SDM79).
source: Expression was constitutive from the endogenous locus and labelling relied on the biotin substate present in the medium (0.8 µM in SDM79) (Moreira do et al., 2023).
evidence: This describes the experimental conditions.

claim: Neither of the bait proteins caused the biotinylation of the entire pore complex.
source: Neither of the bait proteins caused the biotinylation of the entire pore complex.
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data analysis.

claim: Highly specific labelling patterns were observed for each bait protein.
source: Instead, we observed highly specific labelling patterns for each bait.
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data analysis.

claim: The central NUP96 biotinylated most nuclear pore proteins with the marked exception of the nuclear basket.
source: While the central NUP96 biotinylated most nuclear pore proteins with the marked exception of the nuclear basket, NUP158, and NUP76 caused biotinylation of specific sub-complexes of the pore and MEX67 labelled NUPs lining the channel of the pore (Moreira do et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data analysis.

claim: NUP158 and NUP76 caused biotinylation of specific sub-complexes of the pore.
source: While the central NUP96 biotinylated most nuclear pore proteins with the marked exception of the nuclear basket, NUP158, and NUP76 caused biotinylation of specific sub-complexes of the pore and MEX67 labelled NUPs lining the channel of the pore (Moreira do et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data analysis.

claim: MEX67 labelled NUPs lining the channel of the pore.
source: While the central NUP96 biotinylated most nuclear pore proteins with the marked exception of the nuclear basket, NUP158, and NUP76 caused biotinylation of specific sub-complexes of the pore and MEX67 labelled NUPs lining the channel of the pore (Moreira do et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data analysis and cited publication.

claim: The labelling radius of TurboID under these conditions is below the size of the nuclear pore.
source: The data show that the labelling radius of TurboID, under these conditions, is below the size of the nuclear pore and thus well below the resolution of light microscopy.
evidence: This is inferred from the specific labelling patterns observed in mass spectrometry data.

claim: The labelling radius of TurboID is well below the resolution of light microscopy.
source: The data show that the labelling radius of TurboID, under these conditions, is below the size of the nuclear pore and thus well below the resolution of light microscopy.
evidence: This is inferred from the specific labelling patterns observed.

claim: For T. brucei NUP132-TurboID-HA, no obvious differences in resolution were observed between antibody-based and streptavidin-based detection.
source: For T. brucei NUP132-TurboID-HA, no obvious differences in resolution were observed between antibody-based and streptavidin-based detection (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: For human NUP88 expressed as N-terminal TurboID-4HA fusion protein in HeLa cells, the signal of anti-HA and of streptavidin appeared highly similar.
source: Likewise, for human NUP88, expressed as N-terminal TurboID-4HA fusion protein in HeLa cells, grown in DMEM medium (relying on the biotin of the serum supplement with a low nanomolar concentration), the signal of anti-HA and of streptavidin appeared highly similar (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Wild-type cells of both trypanosomes and humans showed only a very low streptavidin signal.
source: Wild-type cells of both trypanosomes and humans showed only a very low streptavidin signal, indicating that the signal from naturally biotinylated proteins is negligible (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The signal from naturally biotinylated proteins is negligible.
source: Wild-type cells of both trypanosomes and humans showed only a very low streptavidin signal, indicating that the signal from naturally biotinylated proteins is negligible (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is inferred from the low background signal in wild-type cells.

claim: Imaging of TurboID fusion proteins via streptavidin is a reliable alternative with a resolution that is indistinguishable from antibody-based immunofluorescence in standard light microscopy.
source: The data demonstrate that imaging of Turbo-ID fusion proteins via streptavidin is a reliable alternative, with a resolution that is indistinguishable from antibody-based immunofluorescence in standard light microscopy, which is in agreement with published data on experimentally determined BioID labeling radii (Branon et al., 2018; Kim et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and cited publications.

claim: Anti-HA failed to stain MEX67 at the nuclear pores.
source: We had previously expressed one of the T. brucei nuclear mRNA transporters, TbMEX67, fused to TurboID-HA and observed that anti-HA failed to stain MEX67 at the nuclear pores, indicating a possible failure of the antibody to either penetrate phase-separated areas or to bind the epitope in this environment (details in introduction, Moreira do et al., 2023, Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 2A and cited publication.

claim: T. brucei nucleolar protein NOG1 fused to C-terminal TurboID-HA showed streptavidin signal exclusively at the nucleolus.
source: We expressed a C-terminal TurboID-HA fusion of the trypanosome nucleolar GTP-binding protein NOG1 (Tb927.11.3120) (Billington et al., 2023). The resulting streptavidin signal was exclusively at the nucleolus, which is tractable as a distinct compartment within the nucleus lacking DAPI fluorescence (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The HA-signal for NOG1 showed no obvious accumulation in the nucleolus and was extremely weak with a patchy distribution throughout the entire cell body.
source: In contrast, the HA-signal showed no obvious accumulation in the nucleolus and was extremely weak with a patchy distribution throughout the entire cell body, indicating an unspecific background stain (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Both anti-HA and streptavidin readily detected starvation stress granules in PABP2-TurboID-HA expressing cells.
source: Both anti-HA and streptavidin readily detected starvation stress granules (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Granules detected by anti-HA were in general less distinct and appeared larger than those detected by streptavidin.
source: However, the granules detected by anti-HA were in general less distinct and appeared larger than those detected by streptavidin.
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data and quantitative analysis.

claim: Intensity profiles drawn through Z-stack projections of stress granules were 1.4±0.2 fold wider for anti-HA detection in comparison to streptavidin detection.
source: Indeed, intensity profiles drawn through Z-stack projections of stress granules were 1.4±0.2 fold wider for anti-HA detection in comparison to streptavidin detection and the corresponding HA profiles frequently exhibited a double-peak (Figure 2D and E).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 2D and E.

claim: Anti-HA preferentially stains the periphery of stress granules, while streptavidin diffuses into and binds within these dense, phase-separated particles.
source: The data are consistent with anti-HA preferentially staining the periphery of the granules, while streptavidin diffuses into and binds within these dense, phase-separated particles.
evidence: This is inferred from the intensity profile data.

claim: Anti-HA fails to label three distinct phase-separated structures of the trypanosome cell: the nuclear pore channel, the nucleolus, and the inside of starvation stress granules.
source: Thus, anti-HA fails to label three distinct phase-separated structures of the trypanosome cell, the nuclear pore channel, the nucleolus, and the inside of starvation stress granules, while streptavidin faithfully decorates all these structures.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on multiple experimental observations.

claim: Streptavidin faithfully decorates the nuclear pore channel, the nucleolus, and the inside of starvation stress granules.
source: Thus, anti-HA fails to label three distinct phase-separated structures of the trypanosome cell, the nuclear pore channel, the nucleolus, and the inside of starvation stress granules, while streptavidin faithfully decorates all these structures.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on multiple experimental observations.

claim: When expressing TurboID-4HA fusions of the human FG-repeat nucleoporin NUP54 in HeLa cells, streptavidin detected the proteins at the nuclear pores, while no specific anti-HA signal was observed.
source: The inability of anti-HA to detect target epitopes within phase-separated areas is not restricted to trypanosomes: When expressing TurboID-4HA fusions of the human FG-repeat nucleoporin NUP54 in HeLa cells, streptavidin detected the proteins at the nuclear pores, while no specific anti-HA signal was observed (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: T. brucei MEX67 and NOG1 fused to TurboID-Ty1 failed to label the nuclear pores and the nucleolus with anti-Ty1 (BB2), respectively.
source: We expressed T. brucei MEX67 and NOG1 fused to TurboID-Ty1 and failed to label the nuclear pores and the nucleolus with anti-Ty1 (BB2), respectively, while the streptavidin signal displayed the correct localisations (Figure 2G and H).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 2G and H.

claim: MEX67 was undetectable at the nuclear pores by polyclonal antiserum.
source: Moreover, MEX67 was undetectable at the nuclear pores by polyclonal antiserum (Figure 2I; Pozzi et al., 2023)
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 2I and cited publication.

claim: An eGFP-fusion of MEX67 could not be detected by fluorophore-labelled eGFP nanobodies at the pores.
source: and an eGFP-fusion of MEX67 could not be detected by fluorophore-labelled eGFP nanobodies at the pores either (Figure 2J).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 2J.

claim: The absence of a nanobody signal rules out that it's simply the size of IgGs that prevents the staining of Mex67 at the nuclear pores.
source: The absence of a nanobody signal rules out that its simply the size of IgGs that prevents the staining of Mex67 at the nuclear pores, as nanobodies are smaller than (tetrameric) streptavidin.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the relative sizes of the detection reagents.

claim: An eGFP fusion of NOG1 was detectable by eGFP nanobodies at the nucleolus, albeit weakly.
source: In contrast, an eGFP fusion of NOG1 was detectable by eGFP nanobodies at the nucleolus, albeit weakly (Figure 2J).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 2J.

claim: TurboID is expected to cause multiple lysine-biotinylation of both the bait protein and proteins in close proximity.
source: A potential advantage for imaging TurboID fusion proteins with streptavidin is an increased signal: TurboID is expected to cause multiple lysine-biotinylation of both the bait protein and proteins in close proximity, while antibodies only decorate several (polyclonals) or one specific (monoclonals) epitope of a target protein.
evidence: This is based on known properties of TurboID.

claim: Antibodies only decorate several (polyclonals) or one specific (monoclonals) epitope of a target protein.
source: A potential advantage for imaging TurboID fusion proteins with streptavidin is an increased signal: TurboID is expected to cause multiple lysine-biotinylation of both the bait protein and proteins in close proximity, while antibodies only decorate several (polyclonals) or one specific (monoclonals) epitope of a target protein.
evidence: This is established knowledge about antibody binding.

claim: For many TurboID-HA fusion proteins, the streptavidin signal appeared significantly stronger and devoid of background stain when compared to anti-HA.
source: Indeed, for many TurboID-HA fusion proteins that we analysed by standard light microscopy, the streptavidin signal appeared significantly stronger and devoid of background stain when compared to anti-HA.
evidence: This is supported by experimental observations.

claim: The streptavidin stain resulted in significantly less non-specific cytoplasmic background signal than anti-HA for NUP158-TurboID-HA.
source: Under both labeling conditions, the streptavidin stain resulted in significantly less non-specific cytoplasmic background signal than anti-HA (Figure 3A–B).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 3A-B.

claim: The maximum Alexa488 signal of Z-stack projections was 2.9-fold higher for streptavidin than for anti-HA (n=60, unpaired two-tailed t-test=9.6E-55).
source: Moreover, the maximum Alexa488 signal of Z-stack projections was 2.9-fold higher for streptavidin than for anti-HA (n=60, unpaired two-tailed t-test=9.6E-55) (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: In expansion microscopy, biomolecules are covalently cross-linked to a hydrogel that is subsequently swollen by osmosis, causing a physical magnification of the sample.
source: In expansion microscopy, biomolecules are covalently cross-linked to a hydrogel, that is subsequently swollen by osmosis, causing a physical magnification of the sample (Chen et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge about expansion microscopy, supported by citation.

claim: A relatively small expansion factor of three causes a 27-fold increase in sample volume and thus a 27-fold decrease in antigen-density.
source: Even a relatively small expansion factor of three causes a 27-fold increase in sample volume and thus a 27-fold decrease in antigen-density.
evidence: This is a mathematical calculation based on the expansion factor.

claim: In proExM, antibody labeling is applied prior to the expansion process.
source: The main difference is that in proExM, antibody labeling is applied prior to the expansion process, while in U-ExM it is done afterward.
evidence: This is established knowledge about expansion microscopy methods.

claim: In U-ExM, antibody labeling is done after the expansion process.
source: The main difference is that in proExM, antibody labeling is applied prior to the expansion process, while in U-ExM it is done afterward.
evidence: This is established knowledge about expansion microscopy methods.

claim: U-ExM generally results in higher resolution than proExM because the linkage-error is not expanded.
source: U-ExM thus generally results in higher resolution, as the linkage-error (difference between the position of the fluorophore of the secondary antibody and the position of the target protein) is not expanded.
evidence: This is established knowledge about expansion microscopy methods.

claim: For both NUP76 and MEX67, streptavidin caused a strong and uniform stain of all nuclear pores with both expansion microscopy methods.
source: For both proteins, streptavidin caused a strong and uniform stain of all nuclear pores with both expansion microscopy methods.
evidence: This is supported by expansion microscopy data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Anti-HA failed to detect nuclear pores completely for MEX67 in U-ExM.
source: In contrast, anti-HA failed to detect nuclear pores either completely (MEX67) or partially (NUP76) in U-ExM.
evidence: This is supported by expansion microscopy data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Anti-HA failed to detect nuclear pores partially for NUP76 in U-ExM.
source: In contrast, anti-HA failed to detect nuclear pores either completely (MEX67) or partially (NUP76) in U-ExM.
evidence: This is supported by expansion microscopy data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: In proExM, pores could be stained evenly with anti-HA, but the signal was much lower in comparison to streptavidin.
source: In proExM, pores could be stained evenly with anti-HA, but the signal was much lower in comparison to streptavidin, in particular for NUP76.
evidence: This is supported by expansion microscopy data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: This is the first time that streptavidin imaging of a biotin ligase-fused protein was used in combination with expansion microscopy.
source: To our knowledge, this is the first time that streptavidin imaging of a biotin ligase-fused protein was used in combination with expansion microscopy.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the approach.

claim: Streptavidin clearly outperformed antibodies in both expansion protocols and with both target proteins tested.
source: In our hands, streptavidin clearly outperformed antibodies in both expansion protocols and with both target proteins that we tested, giving a significantly stronger signal with less background.
evidence: This is supported by expansion microscopy data.

claim: CLEM causes an even larger reduction in accessible antigens than expansion microscopy.
source: CLEM causes an even larger reduction in accessible antigens than expansion microscopy.
evidence: This is based on the nature of the CLEM technique.

claim: In CLEM, the resin largely prevents antibody penetration and probing is restricted to the small fraction of antigens present at the surface of the resin slice.
source: The resin largely prevents antibody penetration and probing is, therefore, restricted to the small fraction of antigens present at the surface of the resin slice.
evidence: This is established knowledge about CLEM methodology.

claim: For both NUP96 and NUP158, the streptavidin signal detected numerous pores for each nucleus in CLEM, while anti-HA detected between 0 and 2 pores.
source: For both proteins, the streptavidin signal detected numerous pores for each nucleus, while anti-HA detected between 0 and 2 pores and, in addition, caused considerably higher background signals (Figure 3E and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by CLEM data shown in Figure 3E and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Anti-HA caused considerably higher background signals than streptavidin in CLEM.
source: For both proteins, the streptavidin signal detected numerous pores for each nucleus, while anti-HA detected between 0 and 2 pores and, in addition, caused considerably higher background signals (Figure 3E and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by CLEM data shown in Figure 3E and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Streptavidin detection causes a massive increase in signal that is particularly beneficial under low-antigen density conditions.
source: In summary, streptavidin detection causes a massive increase in signal that is in particularly beneficial under low-antigen density conditions, and thus offers significant implications in expansion microscopy and CLEM.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on experimental observations.

claim: In most cases, streptavidin labeling faithfully reflects the steady-state localisation of a bait protein.
source: We found that in most cases, streptavidin labeling faithfully reflects the steady-state localisation of a bait protein, e.g., the localisation resembles those observed with immunofluorescence or direct fluorescence imaging of GFP-fusion proteins.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations across multiple proteins.

claim: For certain bait proteins, streptavidin labeling does not reflect steady-state localisation if the bait protein or its interactors have a dynamic localisation to distinct compartments.
source: For certain bait proteins, this is not the case, for example, if the bait protein or its interactors have a dynamic localisation to distinct compartments, or if interactions are highly transient.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations and logical reasoning.

claim: It is essential to control streptavidin-based de novo localisation data by either antibody labelling or by direct fluorescence of fusion-proteins for each new bait protein.
source: It is thus essential to control streptavidin-based de novo localisation data by either antibody labelling (if possible) or by direct fluorescence of fusion-proteins for each new bait protein.
evidence: This is a methodological recommendation based on the findings.

claim: PABP2 has established, unambiguous cytoplasmic localisation when visualised with either anti-HA or when expressed fused to a fluorescent protein.
source: The first is PABP2, one of two trypanosome poly(A) binding proteins, that has established, unambiguous cytoplasmic localisation, when visualised with either anti-HA or when expressed fused to a fluorescent protein (Figure 4A–B; Billington et al., 2023; Kramer et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data and cited publications.

claim: When PABP2-TurboID-HA expressing cells are probed with streptavidin, a signal at the posterior pole of the cell is observed, in addition to the expected cytoplasmic signal.
source: However, when PABP2-TurboID-HA expressing cells are probed with streptavidin, a signal at the posterior pole of the cell is observed, in addition to the expected cytoplasmic signal (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Localisation to the posterior pole is an exclusive feature of the trypanosome mRNA decapping enzyme ALPH1 and its four interaction partners.
source: Localisation to the posterior pole is an exclusive feature of the trypanosome mRNA decapping enzyme ALPH1 and its four interaction partners: a small proportion of this mRNA decapping complex localises to the posterior pole, in a dynamic manner, while the majority remains cytoplasmic (Kramer, 2017; Kramer et al., 2008; Kramer et al., 2023; Figure 4B).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by cited publications and microscopy data.

claim: The streptavidin signal at the posterior pole of the PABP2-TurboID-HA cells likely reflects a historic cytoplasmic interaction between PABP2 and the mRNA decapping complex.
source: The streptavidin signal at the posterior pole of the PABP2-TurboID-HA cells thus likely reflects a historic cytoplasmic interaction between PABP2 and the mRNA decapping complex.
evidence: This is inferred from the localisation pattern and known protein interactions.

claim: All five posterior-pole localised members of the decapping complex were identified by mass spectrometry data from a PABP2 BioID experiment.
source: The existence of this interaction is supported by the identification of all five posterior-pole localised members of the decapping complex by mass spectrometry data from a PABP2 BioID experiment (Moreira do et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data from cited publication.

claim: Imaging with streptavidin shows that the fraction of mRNA decapping proteins at the posterior pole is dynamically exchanged with the fraction in the cytoplasm.
source: Notably, imaging with streptavidin adds information about protein dynamic interactions, that mass spectrometry data alone cannot uncover. In this case, it shows that the fraction of mRNA decapping proteins at the posterior pole is dynamically exchanged with the fraction in the cytoplasm.
evidence: This is inferred from the streptavidin labeling pattern.

claim: MLP2 (also called NUP92) is a divergent nucleoporin of Kinetoplastida involved in chromosome distribution during mitosis.
source: The second example is MLP2 (also called NUP92), a divergent nucleoporin of Kinetoplastida involved in chromosome distribution during mitosis (Holden et al., 2014; Morelle et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by cited publications.

claim: MLP2 localisation is cell cycle-dependent: it exhibits nuclear localisation during interphase and migrates to the spindle and spindle pole during mitosis.
source: MLP2 localisation is cell cycle-dependent: while exhibiting a nuclear localisation during interphase, it migrates to the spindle and spindle pole during mitosis (Holden et al., 2014; Morelle et al., 2015; Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by cited publications and microscopy data.

claim: The streptavidin signal 'lagged behind' the anti-HA signal at all cell cycle stages for MLP2.
source: We observed that the streptavidin signal 'lagged behind' the anti-HA signal at all cell cycle stages.
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: In anaphase, anti-HA exclusively stains the spindle pole body for MLP2, while streptavidin decorates both the nuclei and the spindle pole body.
source: This is most obvious in anaphase, when anti-HA exclusively stains the spindle pole body, while streptavidin decorates both, the nuclei and the spindle pole body.
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: For proteins with cell-cycle dependent localisation, streptavidin-labelling provides information on both the previous localisation(s) of the bait and its current position.
source: Thus, for proteins with cell-cycle dependent localisation, streptavidin-labelling provides information on both, the previous localisation(s) of the bait, in addition to its current position.
evidence: This is inferred from the MLP2 data.

claim: For all NUPs tested, the expected streptavidin signal at the nuclear pores was observed.
source: For all NUPs that we tested, we observed the expected streptavidin signal at the nuclear pores (see below).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data.

claim: For some NUPs, additional cytoplasmic streptavidin stain was observed that is absent for others.
source: However, for some NUPs, for example, NUP65, we observed additional cytoplasmic streptavidin stain that is absent for others, as for example NUP75 (Figure 4D–E).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 4D-E.

claim: There were differences in the amount of nucleoplasmic biotinylation between NUPs.
source: There were also differences in the amount of nucleoplasmic biotinylation between NUPs. For example, NUP75 showed more nuclear labelling than NUP65 (Figure 4D–E).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 4D-E.

claim: Some NUPs are contacting and thus proximity-labelling proteins in transit.
source: The likeliest explanation is, that some NUPs are contacting and thus proximity-labelling proteins in transit.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential labeling patterns.

claim: The streptavidin stain in the nucleoplasm or cytoplasm provides information about the functions of the individual NUPs in protein import or export, respectively.
source: The streptavidin stain in the nucleoplasm or cytoplasm thus provides information about the functions of the individual NUPs in protein import or export, respectively.
evidence: This is inferred from the labeling patterns.

claim: All known trypanosome nuclear pore proteins were endogenously expressed fused to TurboID-HA from one allele.
source: We endogenously expressed all known trypanosome nuclear pore proteins fused to TurboID-HA from one allele.
evidence: This describes the experimental design.

claim: For each nuclear pore protein, two cell lines were constructed, one with TurboID-HA fused to the C-terminus, and one with the tag at the N-terminus.
source: For each protein, two cell lines were constructed, one with TurboID-HA fused to the C-terminus, and one with the tag at the N-terminus.
evidence: This describes the experimental design.

claim: Mlp2/Nup92 was excluded because it localizes to the nucleus rather than the nuclear pores in most interphase cells.
source: We excluded Mlp2/Nup92, as we found this protein localizing to the nucleus rather than the nuclear pores in most interphase cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1 and Figure 4C), in agreement with (Morelle et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data and cited publication.

claim: For two C-terminal fusion candidate proteins (Sec13, NUP140) and one N-terminal (NUP82), cell lines could not be obtained.
source: For two C-terminal fusion candidate proteins (Sec13, NUP140) and one N-terminal (NUP82), we repeatedly failed to obtain cell lines.
evidence: This describes experimental limitations.

claim: All 45 cell lines showed streptavidin signals predominantly at the nuclear pores, proving the correct localisation of the fusion proteins.
source: All cell lines showed streptavidin signals predominantly at the nuclear pores, proving the correct localisation of the fusion proteins (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: For N-terminally tagged NUP64, between one and two streptavidin dots were observed in the nucleus, consistent with the localisation of eYFP-NUP64 in live cells.
source: For N-terminally tagged NUP64 we also observed between one and two streptavidin dots in the nucleus, consistent with the localisation of eYFP-NUP64 in life cells (Billington et al., 2023); a likely mislocalisation.
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data and cited publication.

claim: All the FG-NUPs of the inner channel were among the non-accessible proteins to anti-HA.
source: All the FG-NUPs of the inner channel (which are known to phase-separate) were among the non-accessible proteins, supporting the idea that the crucial determinant preventing anti-HA detection is mainly or entirely phase separation.
evidence: This is supported by the antibody-accessibility mapping data.

claim: The crucial determinant preventing anti-HA detection is mainly or entirely phase separation.
source: All the FG-NUPs of the inner channel (which are known to phase-separate) were among the non-accessible proteins, supporting the idea that the crucial determinant preventing anti-HA detection is mainly or entirely phase separation.
evidence: This is inferred from the correlation between FG-NUPs and antibody inaccessibility.

claim: The mRNA-interacting NUP76 complex consisting of NUP76 and the FG NUPs NUP140 and NUP149 appear non-accessible to anti-HA, except when NUP149 is tagged at the N-terminus.
source: Likewise, the mRNA-interacting NUP76 complex consisting of NUP76 and the FG NUPs NUP140 and NUP149 appear non-accessible to anti-HA, except when NUP149 is tagged at the N-terminus.
evidence: This is supported by the antibody-accessibility mapping data.

claim: NUP158 was inaccessible to antibodies when tagged at the N-terminus, but not at the C-terminus.
source: The NUP76 interacting protein NUP158 was inaccessible to antibodies when tagged at the N-terminus, but not at the C-terminus: this is consistent with NUP158 being partially phase-separated as it contains FG-repeats exclusively at the N-terminal half.
evidence: This is supported by the antibody-accessibility mapping data.

claim: NUP158 contains FG-repeats exclusively at the N-terminal half.
source: The NUP76 interacting protein NUP158 was inaccessible to antibodies when tagged at the N-terminus, but not at the C-terminus: this is consistent with NUP158 being partially phase-separated as it contains FG-repeats exclusively at the N-terminal half.
evidence: This is structural information about NUP158.

claim: Among the antibody-inaccessible proteins were some non-FG NUPs including proteins of the inner ring (NUP181, NUP144, C-terminally tagged NUP225, and N-terminally tagged NUP65) and N-terminally tagged proteins of the outer ring (NUP89 and NUP41).
source: Among the antibody-inaccessible proteins were also some non-FG NUPs. These include proteins of the inner ring, NUP181, NUP144, C-terminally tagged NUP225, and N-terminally tagged NUP65, as well as N-terminally tagged proteins of the outer ring, NUP89 and NUP41.
evidence: This is supported by the antibody-accessibility mapping data.

claim: There is no correlation between protein abundance and immunofluorescence signal for nucleoporins.
source: Importantly, there is no correlation between protein abundance, as determined by proteomics (Tinti and Ferguson, 2022), and immunofluorescence signal, ruling out low antigen abundance as the reason for its absence (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: The use of the TurboID-HA tandem tag offers an 'all in one' solution to antibody-accessibility problems.
source: We here show that the use of the TurboID-HA tandem tag offers an 'all in one' solution to antibody-accessibility problems, without compromising resolution or the strength of the signal.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on all experimental findings.

claim: Streptavidin imaging of TurboID-HA tagged proteins does not compromise resolution or the strength of the signal.
source: We here show that the use of the TurboID-HA tandem tag offers an 'all in one' solution to antibody-accessibility problems, without compromising resolution or the strength of the signal.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data.

claim: Streptavidin imaging facilitates a massive boost in signal, extending the benefits to protein targets with low antigen abundance.
source: Quite the contrary, streptavidin imaging of TurboID-HA tagged proteins facilitates a massive boost in signal, extending the benefits of the method to protein targets with low antigen abundance.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data.

claim: The TurboID-HA tag is suitable for probing protein interactions.
source: Furthermore, the TurboID-HA tag is suitable for probing protein interactions and provides some evidence for phase-separation.
evidence: This is supported by experimental examples.

claim: The TurboID-HA tag provides some evidence for phase-separation.
source: Furthermore, the TurboID-HA tag is suitable for probing protein interactions and provides some evidence for phase-separation.
evidence: This is supported by the antibody-accessibility mapping data.

claim: It is essential to validate both the function and localisation of the TurboID-HA tagged protein by orthogonal methods.
source: Like many methods that are frequently used in cell- and molecular biology, streptavidin imaging is based on the expression of a genetically engineered fusion protein: it is essential to validate both, the function and localisation of the TurboID-HA tagged protein by orthogonal methods.
evidence: This is a methodological recommendation.

claim: The labelling radius of the biotin ligase BirA was estimated to be approximately 10 nm by using the NUP107-160 Y-complex of the mammalian nuclear pore as a molecular ruler.
source: The labelling radius of the biotin ligase BirA was estimated to be approximately 10 nm by using the NUP107-160 Y-complex of the mammalian nuclear pore as a molecular ruler (Kim et al., 2014), enabling, for example, the determination of substructures of P-bodies and stress granules (Youn et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The labelling radius of BirA is within the range of an average-sized protein and well below the resolution limit of light microscopy.
source: It is thus within the range of an average-sized protein and well below the resolution limit of light microscopy.
evidence: This is inferred from the measured labelling radius.

claim: For the biotin ligase variant TurboID, the biotin labelling radius was measured to be in a similar or slightly larger range than BirA.
source: For the biotin ligase variant TurboID, which has a massively decreased labelling time, the biotin labelling radius was measured to be in a similar (Branon et al., 2018; Kim et al., 2016) or slightly larger range (May et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The addition of 50 µM external biotin massively increased the labelling radius of TurboID.
source: Importantly, the addition of 50 µM external biotin massively increased the labelling radius, while in the absence of excessive biotin, the labelling radius remained comparable to the labelling radius of BirA (May et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: In the absence of excessive biotin, the labelling radius of TurboID remained comparable to the labelling radius of BirA.
source: Importantly, the addition of 50 µM external biotin massively increased the labelling radius, while in the absence of excessive biotin, the labelling radius remained comparable to the labelling radius of BirA (May et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Additional biotin was not added to the trypanosome medium in this work.
source: In this work, we avoided the addition of additional biotin to the trypanosome medium (the medium contains 0.8 µM biotin) and serum biotin (approximately 2 nM in mammalian serum Luong and Vashist, 2020) was the sole source in HeLa cell medium.
evidence: This describes the experimental conditions.

claim: Serum biotin (approximately 2 nM in mammalian serum) was the sole source in HeLa cell medium.
source: In this work, we avoided the addition of additional biotin to the trypanosome medium (the medium contains 0.8 µM biotin) and serum biotin (approximately 2 nM in mammalian serum Luong and Vashist, 2020) was the sole source in HeLa cell medium.
evidence: This describes the experimental conditions and cites a source for serum biotin concentration.

claim: Mass spectrometry data demonstrates that the labeling radius is well below the size of the nuclear pore complex under the conditions used.
source: Our mass spectrometry data of streptavidin-affinity purified proteins with five nuclear pore-localised TurboID-fusion proteins demonstrates that the labeling radius is well below the size of the nuclear pore complex under these conditions, and thus in agreement with published data.
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data analysis.

claim: In expansion microscopy with 3.6–4.2-fold expansion factors, no decrease in resolution was noticed for streptavidin imaging.
source: Even in expansion microscopy, with 3.6–4.2-fold expansion factors, we did not notice any decrease in resolution; in fact, we could resolve NUPs that reside at different positions within the pore (e.g. inner ring vs basket) by labeling one with streptavidin and the other with an antibody and thus obtained sub-NUP imaging resolution (our own unpublished data).
evidence: This is supported by unpublished experimental data.

claim: Sub-NUP imaging resolution was obtained by labeling one NUP with streptavidin and another with an antibody in expansion microscopy.
source: Even in expansion microscopy, with 3.6–4.2-fold expansion factors, we did not notice any decrease in resolution; in fact, we could resolve NUPs that reside at different positions within the pore (e.g. inner ring vs basket) by labeling one with streptavidin and the other with an antibody and thus obtained sub-NUP imaging resolution (our own unpublished data).
evidence: This is supported by unpublished experimental data.

claim: BioID per se causes a decrease in resolution as biotinylation extends to proteins in close proximity to the bait.
source: Even though, theoretically, BioID per se causes a decrease in resolution as biotinylation extends to proteins in close proximity to the bait, this may well be compensated by the lower linkage error when imaging directly via the small, compact-shaped streptavidin-tetramer rather than by a tandem assembly of two large IgG antibodies (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a theoretical consideration based on the nature of proximity labeling.

claim: The decrease in resolution from BioID may be compensated by the lower linkage error when imaging via streptavidin compared to IgG antibodies.
source: Even though, theoretically, BioID per se causes a decrease in resolution as biotinylation extends to proteins in close proximity to the bait, this may well be compensated by the lower linkage error when imaging directly via the small, compact-shaped streptavidin-tetramer rather than by a tandem assembly of two large IgG antibodies (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a theoretical consideration based on the sizes of detection reagents.

claim: Fluorescent streptavidin has been previously used in expansion microscopy to detect biotin residues in target proteins produced by click chemistry.
source: Fluorescent streptavidin has been previously used in expansion microscopy to detect biotin residues in target proteins produced by click chemistry (Sun et al., 2021).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: This is the first report that employs fluorescent streptavidin as a signal enhancer in expansion microscopy and CLEM by combining it with multiple biotinylation sites added by a biotin ligase.
source: However, to the best of our knowledge, this is the first report that employs fluorescent streptavidin as a signal enhancer in expansion microscopy and CLEM, by combining it with multiple biotinylation sites added by a biotin ligase.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the approach.

claim: For both CLEM and expansion microscopy, streptavidin imaging is the only alternative approach to immunofluorescence, as denaturing conditions rule out direct imaging of fluorescent tags.
source: Importantly, for both CLEM and expansion, streptavidin imaging is the only alternative approach to immunofluorescence, as denaturing conditions associated with these methods rule out direct imaging of fluorescent tags.
evidence: This is based on the nature of the imaging methods.

claim: The importance of compartmentalisation by liquid-liquid phase separation for almost all cellular functions becomes increasingly evident.
source: The importance of compartmentalisation by liquid-liquid phase separation for almost all cellular functions, including DNA and mRNA metabolism (Dai and Yang, 2024), cell division (Ong and Torres, 2020), and development (So et al., 2021) becomes increasingly evident.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Aberrant phase separation can cause disease, such as neurodegenerative disorders.
source: Aberrant phase separation can cause disease, as for example neurodegenerative disorders (Chakraborty and Zweckstetter, 2023; Tsoi et al., 2023), underlining the relevance of novel tools for the identification and characterisation of phase-separated regions.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: For individual proteins, phase separation can be predicted in silico using machine learning, with limited but increasing accuracy.
source: For individual proteins, phase separation can be predicted in silico using machine learning, with limited, but increasing accuracy (Venko and Žerovnik, 2023).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: For a defined mixture of molecules, phase separation can be tested in vitro.
source: For a defined mixture of molecules, phase separation can be tested in vitro (Alberti et al., 2018; Zhang and Shen, 2023).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Methods to test phase separation in the cellular context are scarce.
source: However, methods to test phase separation in the cellular context are scarce.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of the field.

claim: The correlation between antibody-inaccessibility and phase separation offers the opportunity to use the TurboID-HA tag to probe for phase separation de novo.
source: The correlation between antibody-inaccessibility and phase separation, that we observed in this study, offers the opportunity to use the TurboID-HA tag to probe for phase separation de novo.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental findings.

claim: The streptavidin stain provides a convenient intrinsic control to confirm the correct localisation of the fusion protein.
source: Notably, the streptavidin stain concomitantly provides a convenient intrinsic control to confirm the correct localisation of the fusion protein.
evidence: This is based on the experimental observations.

claim: Proteins with complex localisation patterns can be simultaneously detected in both phase-separated and non-phase-separated regions using streptavidin.
source: Moreover, proteins with complex localisation patterns can be simultaneously detected in both, phase-separated and non-phase-separated regions, as we demonstrated for tracing MEX67 to both, the nucleoplasm and nuclear pores (Figure 1A and G).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data.

claim: In trypanosomes, all bona fide phase-separated regions were inaccessible to anti-HA.
source: In trypanosomes, all bona fide phase-separated regions were inaccessible to anti-HA, namely the nucleolus, starvation stress granules, and the FG NUP environment.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data.

claim: The absence of an HA immunofluorescence signal strongly suggests correlation with phase-separation.
source: The data strongly suggest that the absence of an HA immunofluorescence signal correlates with phase-separation.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental findings.

claim: Some proteins may be inaccessible to anti-HA for different reasons, such as steric hindrance.
source: However, we cannot rule out the possibility, that some proteins may be inaccessible to anti-HA for different reasons, as for example steric hindrance.
evidence: This is a consideration of alternative explanations.

claim: Steric hindrance would equally favor streptavidin over IgG antibodies for target protein binding due to its much smaller dimensions and higher binding affinity.
source: The latter scenario would equally favor streptavidin over IgG antibodies for target protein binding due to its much smaller dimensions and higher binding affinity.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the properties of the detection reagents.

claim: Problems to detect phase-separated proteins by antibodies appear conserved across species.
source: Importantly, problems to detect phase-separated proteins by antibodies appear conserved across species (Bear et al., 1999; Misteli, 2008; Musinova et al., 2011; Sheval et al., 2005; Zatsepina et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by multiple cited publications.

claim: The de novo identification of phase-separation using TurboID-HA is applicable to human cells.
source: We show data for the human FG-NUP Nup54 as an example of an anti-HA-inaccessible protein (Figure 2F) as proof of principle, that the de novo identification of phase-separation is applicable to human cells.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: The smaller size of streptavidin in comparison to an IgG tandem-antibody pair likely favors its access into dense regions.
source: Still, the smaller size of streptavidin in comparison to an IgG tandem-antibody pair (Figure 1b) likely favors its access into dense regions.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the relative sizes.

claim: IgG antibodies typically have affinities in the nanomolar range.
source: Furthermore, IgG antibodies as well as single-chain antibodies typically have affinities in the nanomolar range, compared to the femtomolar affinity of the biotin-streptavidin interaction, which is indeed among the strongest non-covalent interactions in nature (Chivers et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: The biotin-streptavidin interaction has femtomolar affinity and is among the strongest non-covalent interactions in nature.
source: Furthermore, IgG antibodies as well as single-chain antibodies typically have affinities in the nanomolar range, compared to the femtomolar affinity of the biotin-streptavidin interaction, which is indeed among the strongest non-covalent interactions in nature (Chivers et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Streptavidin has extremely high structural stability towards temperature, pH, and denaturing conditions.
source: Together with the extremely high structural stability of streptavidin towards temperature, pH, and denaturing conditions (Laitinen et al., 2006) this can explain the ability of this probe to potently outperform antibodies in phase-separated environments.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Streptavidin imaging is proposed as a novel tool to monitor dynamic interactions between proteins.
source: Lastly, we propose streptavidin imaging as a novel tool to monitor dynamic interactions between proteins.
evidence: This is based on the experimental examples provided.

claim: BioID proximity labeling extends to all interacting partners, preserving the history of interactions.
source: Since BioID proximity labeling is not restricted to the bait protein, but extends to all interacting partners, the history of interactions is preserved.
evidence: This is based on known properties of BioID and experimental observations.

claim: Changes in protein sub-complexes can be imaged over time using streptavidin imaging.
source: Hence, changes in protein sub-complexes can be imaged over time.
evidence: This is inferred from the properties of biotinylation and experimental examples.

claim: A tightly controlled, inducible system such as Split-TurboID in combination with light activation would allow pulse-chase experiments.
source: While we relied on an endogenous, constitutive expression of TurboID fusion proteins, a tightly controlled, inducible system, as for example, Split-TurboID (Cho et al., 2020) in combination with light activation (Chen et al., 2022; Shafraz et al., 2023) would allow pulse-chase experiment, delivering quantitative data on the kinetics of processes.
evidence: This is a proposal for future applications, supported by citations.

claim: Streptavidin imaging is a highly versatile tool with multiple applications.
source: Altogether, streptavidin imaging is a highly versatile tool with multiple applications, ranging from a simple boost in a signal that can be leveraged to increase imaging sensitivity in expansion microscopy and CLEM, to the ability to probe for phase-separated areas and to monitor dynamic protein interactions.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on all experimental findings.

claim: Streptavidin imaging is an important addition to the available imaging toolbox.
source: It is thus an important addition to the available imaging toolbox.
evidence: This is a concluding statement based on the demonstrated applications.
